thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — staging image scan just flagged a high severity openssl vuln in our base image (CVE-2026-2400). Rebuild candidate is queued but we need RBAC/KMS sign-off before we push.
jonathan: Ugh. Is that in the distro package or a vendored lib?
maria: distro package (debian:bullseye-slim -> openssl 1.1.1k). SBOM attached in thread below. :grimacing:
ashley: @maria can you paste the SBOM snippet and the exact layer hash? We need to know if rebuilding the base will address, or if app layer pins a vulnerable binary.
maria: SBOM snippet:
```
openssl 1.1.1k layer sha256:9f8a... pkgmgr:apt
component-path: /usr/lib/ssl
```
maria: layer hash -> sha256:9f8a7b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a
kevin: Ok. Two parallel asks: 1) Can we rebuild base image with patched openssl and sign it via KMS? 2) Temporarily grant the rebuild runner a key-encrypt role to upload signed artifact.
ashley: For (2) +1 but let's scope RBAC tight: create a short-lived role image-rebuild-runner with only cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign or equivalent, and only for the dedicated keystore.
jonathan: Also need audit trail: who requested and who triggered the sign. Audit logs must include CryptoKeyEncrypt/CryptoKeySign events. Anyone seen our previous snippets for audit policy?
kevin: Yep — ensure Cloud Audit Logs for the KMS key are enabled (ADMIN_READ and DATA_WRITE). We can integrate with our central logging sink so image sign events generate an alert in the image-trust-runbook. I can add the log filter:
```
resource.type="kms_key"
logName="projects/redwood-prod/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity"
protoPayload.methodName:"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign"
```
kevin: That will bubble to the security-alerts channel.
ashley: One more: CI runner will need ephemeral credentials to access the keystore. Use short-lived signing tokens from our OIDC broker rather than long-lived service account keys.
maria: CI plan: rebuild base -> run full image-scan -> publish signed artifact to staging-registry. Can someone draft the minimal IAM policy we need? I'll block the pipeline until roles exist.
jonathan: Draft policy idea (minimal):
- principals: service account:ci-image-rebuilder@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- roles: kms.signer (custom with only AsymmetricSign), storage.objectCreator for staging-bucket, logging.logWriter
- condition: request.time < timestamp("+1h") on the temporary role
ashley: Condition-based binding looks good. For GCP we can set a temporary IAM binding via IAMCredentials.generateAccessToken or set a time-bound binding via the API. I can automate in the rebuild job.
kevin: Security note: audit logs are only useful if we also capture the signer metadata. Add environment variables to the pipeline that stamp BUILD_ID, USER_TRIGGER, and GIT_COMMIT into the image label so we can correlate.
sre-bot: [CI] rebuild-job-#482 queued by maria — scanned layers: 14, pending: sign step. ETA ~12m.
maria: Thanks. Also tagging @oncall since this touches signing keys: @kevin please confirm key rotation status and if we need a new key for the patch roll.
kevin: Key rotation: primary key is active and rotated last month. No need to rotate for this patch. If you want isolation, create a signing subkey 'rebuild-2026-03' scoped to staging only. I'll create it if you ask.
maria: Let's create the subkey. Also, can we have an emergency revoke path if the rebuild runner is compromised?
ashley: Yes — keep a manual revocation SOP in the runbook: revoke key, blacklist image digest at registry, invalidate CI tokens, and rollback to previous runtime pin. I'll update runbook.
jonathan: Vulnerability triage: is there a workaround (recompile, patch) to avoid full base rebuild now?
maria: temporary mitigation: pin app to use system openssl via ldpreload shim -> not great. Prefer rebuild to ensure forward fixes and smaller blast radius.
kevin: I will provision subkey + create time-bound IAM binding. Expecting to push policy in ~30m. I'll post the exact IAM JSON when done.
maria: Perfect. When the signed artifact lands in staging, I'll run canary roll and trigger the security smoke tests. Report back here with sign event ID so we can close the loop.
ashley: Added tasks to the image-trust runbook: create-subkey, bind-rebuild-runner, enable-kms-audit-filter, stamp-image-metadata, revoke-procedure.
jonathan: Thanks everyone. After this I'll open a minimal PR to update the base Dockerfile and kick off the rebuilt pipeline.
maria: :thumbsup: closing the loop — will ping when sign event present.
kevin: Posted IAM JSON and KMS subkey name in a follow-up message (see log). :lock:
maria: sgtm. Moving pipeline to blocked->running. :rocket:
